stem.en: Which statement about mitosis is correct?

text.en: It gives two cells with the same number of chromosomes.

feedback.en: Yes. Each daughter cell has the same number as the parent cell.

text.en: It gives two cells, each with half the parent's chromosomes.

feedback.en: Halving the number happens in a different division, which comes next.

text.en: It gives one larger cell with twice the chromosomes.

feedback.en: Mitosis gives two cells, and the number does not double.

text.en: It gives four cells of slightly different kinds.

feedback.en: Mitosis gives two cells, and they are identical to the parent.

explanation.en: Every chromosome is copied, and the copies separate into two daughter cells. Each has the same number of chromosomes as the parent, so the offspring are clones.

hints.en: Count the chromosomes before and after.
